Middle East Referral Project — Service Evaluation

Every call, one page away.

This is the working script library for the TMK Service Evaluation team — the same scripts, translated into the branching logic every call actually follows, with a worked call sample under each one.

Training · Welcome

Welcome to the TMK Service Evaluation Project

This handbook is designed for existing TMK team members. It explains not only what to do during every service evaluation call, but why this project exists, why TMK was selected, and how your work contributes to customer experience and referral growth.

Why was this project created?

The former CM model proved that service evaluation conversations naturally generate high-quality referrals. This project rebuilds that model by focusing on service evaluation, issue resolution, and referral activation only after customer satisfaction is confirmed.

Why TMK?

  • The team has demonstrated efficient and reliable work, with the ability to execute tasks in an organized and effective way.
  • The team already understands 51Talk products and the customer experience, enabling more effective user interactions.
  • The team can integrate quickly with existing projects and support them without building a new team from scratch.

Your Mission

  • Evaluate the customer's learning experience.
  • Identify satisfaction and service issues.
  • Resolve issues whenever possible.
  • Turn satisfied users into referral opportunities naturally by asking at the right moment and in the right way.
  • Capture and follow up on high-quality referrals to drive attendance and conversion, rather than focusing only on referral volume.

Project Philosophy

Service → Trust → Satisfaction → Referral → Attendance → Growth

A referral is not the objective of the call—it is the natural outcome of an excellent customer experience.

What We Expect From Every TMK Member

  • Put customer experience first.
  • Listen before recommending.
  • Resolve before escalating whenever possible.
  • Encourage the customer to make a referral, but never force or pressure them.
  • Document every interaction accurately.
  • Represent the Service Evaluation Team professionally.
Training · Start Here

Why This Project Exists

Across the Middle East, there's a structural gap in referrals: the original CM team proved that service calls naturally trigger referrals, but the newer SS team's reach alone can't sustain that same level of output.

~40
referral leads per CM agent, historically
~4
orders generated per CM agent

This isn't a new experiment starting from zero — it's a proven model. The real work is fixing the surrounding pieces: onboarding, performance appraisal, service-access permissions, and standardized process.

So the core of this project isn't "add a team that asks for referrals." It's building a service-evaluation team dedicated to paying users — one that identifies satisfaction, resolves real issues, and lets high-quality referrals happen as a natural result.

★

The Project Goal

The goal is to build a complete service workflow that turns customer-experience evaluation into real issue resolution, followed by high-quality referrals only after customer satisfaction is confirmed.

01

Improve Customer Experience

Identify issues early, resolve them within available permissions, and escalate cases that require additional support.

02

Generate Quality Referrals

Ask satisfied customers for referrals naturally and without pressure, focusing on attendance and conversion quality.

03

Build a Closed Follow-up Loop

Document every interaction and follow resolution, satisfaction, and referral outcomes until completion or clear reassignment.

★

Your Role — Five Responsibilities

Everything in the script library maps back to these five responsibilities. Understanding the "why" behind each one makes the scripts easier to use naturally.

1

Service Experience Evaluation

Run service-evaluation calls with paying users to assess their recent learning experience: course schedule, teacher satisfaction, service responsiveness, attendance, overall satisfaction.

2

Handling Dissatisfied Users

If a user is dissatisfied, don't just log it — you're empowered to actually resolve it. Prioritize fixing the issue before deciding whether a referral is appropriate.

If a call can only log a problem without fixing it, the experience won't improve — and word-of-mouth referrals won't happen.

3

Referral Trigger from Satisfied Users

For users with high satisfaction, stable learning experience, and no complaints, the trigger follows a natural chain: confirm experience → assess satisfaction → reinforce learning value → naturally ask about friends or relatives → capture the referral → follow up on attendance and conversion.

4

Check-in / Share Fallback

If a user is satisfied but can't name a referral right now, guide them to at least one check-in or share. It keeps them engaged, adds natural exposure, creates future referral opportunities, and removes the pressure of needing a referral on every single call.

5

Accurate Logging & Follow-up

Record every call outcome, satisfaction level, issue type, resolution or escalation status, referral result, and next action. Follow open cases until they are closed or clearly assigned to the responsible owner.

  1. User list is entered into the system and TMK checks the user's status and service context.
  2. Make the first call and determine whether it is answered.
  3. If the call is not answered, do not start the service-evaluation flow. Send the approved WhatsApp time-booking message and arrange a suitable callback.
  4. If the call is answered, continue with the existing Opening & Service Evaluation process.
  5. Assess the customer's satisfaction before discussing referrals.
  6. If the customer is satisfied, arrange/perform the referral follow-up call and ask for a referral naturally and without pressure.
  7. If the customer is dissatisfied, identify the issue and attempt to resolve it within TMK permissions.
  8. If the issue cannot be resolved within TMK authority, escalate it to the relevant department or owner.
  9. After the issue is resolved, follow up with the customer to confirm that the solution worked and that the customer is satisfied.
  10. If satisfaction is confirmed, make the referral follow-up call and ask for a referral.
  11. If the customer is still dissatisfied, continue the resolution/escalation process and follow up again until the required action is completed.
  12. If there is no referral, use the approved check-in/share fallback where applicable rather than pressuring the customer.
  13. Log every interaction accurately, including call outcome, satisfaction, issue, resolution/escalation, post-resolution follow-up, referral result, and next action.
  14. Close the case only when all required actions are completed or the remaining follow-up is clearly documented and assigned.
Core rule: Service evaluation → Issue resolution when needed → Satisfaction confirmation → Referral follow-up → Referral / check-in / share → Logging & follow-up.

Referral must never replace service recovery. A dissatisfied customer should be helped first. After the issue is resolved, satisfaction must be confirmed before the referral request.
★

How You'll Be Measured

Deliberately, "number of referrals" is not the core metric. Chasing raw referral counts leads to low-quality leads and unnecessary interruption of users — so performance shifts from "how many" to "do they actually show up."

Indicator typeIndicatorPurposeStatus
Outcome (North Star)Referral attendance targetEnsures quality of referrals, not just registration countAvailable
OutcomeCheck-in participation rateEnsures users can contribute even without a referralNot Available
ProcessValid call volume, answer rate, evaluation completion rateEnsures basic activity and coverageAvailable
ServiceIssue resolution rate, escalation timeliness, satisfactionEnsures the team genuinely serves, not just refersAvailable
ConversionAttendance rate, attendance-payment rate, referral-payment rateAssesses business contribution of referralsAvailable

Two incentive tiers

Tier 1 — process incentives: built around effective call volume, evaluation completion, check-in participation, and issue-resolution completion.

Tier 2 — outcome incentives: built around referral attendance, post-attendance paid contribution, and valid order contribution.

The goal: make it worthwhile to both make the calls and register high-quality referrals — without chasing referral counts alone.

What Success Looks Like in Phase 1

The goal isn't to scale up production immediately — it's to prove the closed loop actually works.

  • Can the service-evaluation call be completed reliably?
  • Can satisfied and dissatisfied users be reliably identified?
  • Can basic service issues actually be resolved?
  • Can high-quality referrals be generated from satisfied users?
  • Can check-ins or shares serve as a reliable fallback?
  • Can referrals convert into attendance and payment?
  • Can the team support the User Experience project alongside this?
Result typeKey indicators
Service coverageCall volume, answer rate, evaluation completion rate
User experienceSatisfaction, issue type, issue resolution rate
Quality of referralsNumber of attendees from referrals, attendance rate, paid-attendance rate
Share participationCheck-in participation rate, share completion rate
★

The Bigger Picture

The value of this project is building a new handover mechanism — service evaluation, issue resolution, high-quality referral triggering, and user-experience accumulation — in a gap the existing team can't fully cover alone.

This isn't about asking TMK to chase referral leads. It's about positioning TMK as a genuine service-evaluation team: assess experience first, fix real problems for dissatisfied users, let satisfied users trigger referrals naturally, and guide everyone else toward a check-in or share.

Service evaluation → Issue resolution → Satisfaction identification → High-quality referrals → Check-in/share fallback → Attendance/payment conversion → User experience accumulation → Continuous iteration.

Step 1 · Answer Decision

Was the Call Answered?

This is the new first decision before the opening. First determine whether the user answered the call. If yes, go directly to the existing Opening & Service Evaluation flow and continue the old workflow unchanged. If no, do not start the service-evaluation flow; send a WhatsApp message to book a suitable callback time.

If YES

YES → Go directly to Step 1: Opening & Service Evaluation, then continue the existing call workflow with no changes.

If NO

NO → Do not enter the opening or satisfaction-assessment flow. Send a WhatsApp message to book a suitable callback time.

WhatsApp — Time Booking

Hello, this is Rania from 51Talk's Service Evaluation team. We tried to reach you to check in on your child's learning experience. We'd like to call at a time that is convenient for you — what time would work best for a callback?

New branch rule: Answered = continue the old workflow from Opening. No answer = WhatsApp time booking; do not enter the old workflow until a suitable callback time is arranged and the call is answered.

Survey → Referral Reference

How to Move From the Survey to the Referral

This reference is specifically for the TMK flow: the customer has completed the survey, confirmed satisfaction, and has no open issue. The goal is to move naturally from satisfaction with the service to showing the customer the personal value of the referral program. These are not scripts to memorize; they are examples of how to build the transition naturally.

The Core Rule

01Confirm satisfaction
→
02Reflect what they liked
→
03Connect it to customer benefit
→
04Introduce referral
→
05Explain reward
→
06Ask permission to continue

Core Transition — After Customer Satisfaction

Recommended approach Core

We’re really happy to hear that you’re enjoying the service and having a good experience with us. Since you’ve had a good experience, I’d like to tell you about another way you can benefit. We have a referral program where you can earn rewards while helping your child continue learning English. You can earn up to 7,000 SAR through cashback and shopping vouchers; cashback is paid directly to your bank account, and the vouchers can be used at more than 200 stores. With 5 successful referrals, the rewards can reach a value that can help cover the cost of your child’s English learning for a year. If you’d like, I can explain how the program works and how you can benefit from the rewards.

Examples Based on the Customer's Survey Answer

If they say: “I’m happy with the teacher.” Teacher

We’re really happy that you’re pleased with the teacher and that the experience is going well. Since you’re happy with the experience, there’s another way you can benefit too — our referral program. You can earn cashback and shopping vouchers when you refer people who are genuinely interested, with rewards of up to 7,000 SAR. Would you like me to explain the details?

If they say: “My child has improved.” Results

That’s great to hear — seeing your child improve is exactly what we want. Since you can see the difference, I wanted to tell you about an opportunity that can benefit you as well. Our referral program gives you cashback and vouchers, and your rewards increase as you make more successful referrals. With 5 successful referrals, the rewards can reach a value that covers your child’s learning cost for a year. Would you like me to explain how it works?

If they say: “The service is excellent.” Service

We’re really happy that you like the service. Since you see the service this way, there’s an additional way you can benefit from your experience with us. Our referral program can give you up to 7,000 SAR through cashback and shopping vouchers. Cashback goes to your bank account, and the vouchers can be used at more than 200 stores. If you’d like, I can explain how you can benefit from it.

If they say: “Everything is good.” Simple

Perfect, that’s exactly what we like to hear. Since everything is going well, I have something you might like. We have a referral program where you can earn rewards for people you refer, with rewards of up to 7,000 SAR. If you’d like, I can give you a quick idea about it?

When the Customer Gives a Short Positive Answer

Perfect, الحمدلله. The most important thing is that you’re happy with the service. By the way, there’s another way you can benefit from your experience — our referral program offers cashback and vouchers, with rewards of up to 7,000 SAR. If you’d like, I can explain it quickly?

When the Customer Mentions Someone or Says They Recommend the Service

That’s great — if you’d recommend the service, we really appreciate it. You also have an opportunity to benefit when someone comes through you. The referral program gives you cashback and shopping vouchers. If you’d like, I can explain how the rewards work and how the referral is registered.

What Makes the Transition Natural?

❤️

Start With the Customer

Do not start with the referral. Start with what the customer just said about their experience.

🔗

Create the Link

Connect satisfaction to a personal benefit: they like the service, and now they can benefit from that experience in another way.

🎁

Show the Value

State the reward clearly, then give a tangible example such as 5 referrals and the value of a year of learning.

Avoid a Sudden Pitch

❌ Don't jump directly to:

“Do you have anyone to refer?”

“We have a referral program, give us some numbers.”

✅ Better:

Confirm satisfaction → connect the experience to a customer benefit → introduce the program → explain the value → ask if they want to know more.

If the Customer Says Yes, Continue

Of course. We have reward levels based on the number of referrals. Cashback goes to your bank account, and the vouchers can be used at more than 200 stores. Shall I explain the levels and how the referral is registered?

If the Customer Is Not Interested

Of course, no problem at all. I just wanted to make you aware of the opportunity. If you ever think about it later, you can contact us.

01

Opening & Service Evaluation

After the new call-answer decision returns YES, confirm identity, set a low-pressure tone, and move into the satisfaction check. Referral is never mentioned here — start with a familiar, short service-focused tone and complete the satisfaction check before discussing referrals.

Opening line

Hello, this is Rania, a Service Evaluation Specialist at 51Talk. Am I speaking with Umm Faisal, parent of Faisal? I'm calling today simply to check in on your child's recent learning experience — it will only take a couple of minutes.

If the parent seems rushed

I understand you're busy — this isn't a sales call, it's a short service check we do for active families. I just have three quick questions and then I'll let you go.

Sample Call — routine openingRecorded 04:12
R
Rania · AgentHello, this is Rania from 51Talk's Service Evaluation team — am I speaking with Umm Faisal?
U
Umm Faisal · ParentYes, speaking. Is everything okay?
R
Rania · AgentEverything's fine — I'm just calling to check how Faisal's classes have been going lately. Do you have two minutes?
U
Umm Faisal · ParentAh, okay — yes, go ahead.

Coaching note: The tone should feel familiar, short, and service-focused in the first 10 seconds.

Move From Service Evaluation to Referral

After the survey, if the customer confirms satisfaction and there is no open issue, this is where the referral conversation begins. Do not jump straight to “Do you have anyone to refer?” Use what the customer just said about their experience as the bridge to the benefit they can receive.

Recommended referral opening after satisfaction Referral

We’re really happy to hear that you’re enjoying the service and having a good experience with us. Since you’ve had a good experience, I’d like to tell you about another way you can benefit. We have a referral program where you can earn rewards while helping your child continue learning English. You can earn up to 7,000 SAR through cashback and shopping vouchers; cashback is paid directly to your bank account, and the vouchers can be used at more than 200 stores. With 5 successful referrals, the rewards can reach a value that can help cover the cost of your child’s English learning for a year. If you’d like, I can explain how the program works and how you can benefit from the rewards.

If the customer praises the teacher: We’re happy that you’re pleased with the teacher. Since your experience has been great, there’s also an opportunity to benefit from our referral program and earn rewards from people you refer. Would you like me to explain?
If the customer says their child improved: That’s great to hear. Since you can see the difference in your child, I wanted to tell you about an opportunity that can benefit you too — our referral program.

Rule: Satisfaction First, Referral Value Second

  1. Complete the survey and confirm the customer is satisfied.
  2. Pick up on a positive point the customer mentioned, such as the teacher, child improvement, or service.
  3. Connect that positive point to a personal benefit for the customer.
  4. Introduce the referral program and rewards clearly.
  5. Use the 5-referral / one-year learning example to make the benefit tangible.
  6. Ask if they would like the details instead of immediately pressuring them for a contact.
02

Satisfaction Assessment Probes

Five dimensions build the standard call output: satisfaction level, main feedback, whether there's an issue, whether referral is appropriate, and whether follow-up is needed. The last question is the branch point.

DimensionProbeListening for
AttendanceHow consistent has attendance been recently?Frequent absences, scheduling conflicts
TeacherHow does your child feel about the current teacher?Rapport, requests to switch
ScheduleDoes the current schedule and level still work well?Overload, mismatch
ResponsivenessWhen you've reached out before, how was the response?Unresolved past tickets
OverallOverall, how would you describe the experience — very satisfied, satisfied, or not satisfied?Direct branch signal

Branch point: a clearly positive answer → Section 3. Any hesitation or complaint → Section 5.

03
Branch A · Satisfied

Referral Trigger Script

Enter only once satisfaction is clearly confirmed and there is no open issue. After the survey, open the referral conversation from the customer's benefit: they are happy with the service, there is another way to benefit from that experience, and the rewards can support their child's continued learning. This is a way of thinking, not a script that must be memorized word for word.

Opening the referral conversation after the satisfaction check

We're really happy to hear that you're enjoying the service and having a good experience with us. Since you've had a good experience, I'd like to tell you about another way you can benefit. We have a referral program where you can earn rewards while helping your child continue learning English. You can earn up to 7,000 SAR through cashback and shopping vouchers; cashback is paid directly to your bank account, and the vouchers can be used at more than 200 stores. With 5 successful referrals, you can cover the value of your child's English learning for a full year. If you'd like, I can explain how the program works and how you can benefit from the rewards.

The thinking, not a word-for-word script

  • Start by confirming the customer's satisfaction and showing that you're happy their experience was good.
  • Connect the referral to a direct customer benefit: rewards that can help them continue their child's learning.
  • State the headline benefit clearly: up to 7,000 SAR through cashback and vouchers.
  • Make the reward tangible: cashback to the bank account and vouchers for 200+ stores.
  • Use the 5-referral example to connect the reward directly to a year's value of the child's learning.
  • After explaining the benefit, ask if the customer would like the details — don't pressure them.

If the customer is interested

Of course. I'll explain the referral levels and rewards and how you can benefit from them step by step.

If the customer names a referral

Great — give me their name and phone number. Our team will contact them and mention that you referred them, and we'll confirm your reward according to the current referral terms.

Sample Call — referral capturedOutcome: Referral logged

U
Umm Faisal · ParentSure, it's Aisha, 05X-XXX-XXXX.
R
Rania · AgentThank you so much — I've noted Aisha as your referral, and our team will follow up within three days.

Never quote a specific reward figure without confirming the referral terms currently in effect.

Branch B · Dissatisfied

Issue Resolution Scripts

The moment dissatisfaction surfaces, stop the evaluation flow and move to resolution. No referral talk in this branch — resolve first, revisit referral potential on a future call.

General acknowledgment

Thank you for letting me know — I want to make sure we get this right for you. Let me look into this and see what I can do directly, or make sure it reaches the right person.

Issue typeScript
Occasional leaveI can process an occasional leave for you now — could you confirm the date(s) and the reason?
Tutoring / extra helpI can arrange a tutoring session to help with that — let me check what's available and get this scheduled.
Schedule adjustmentI can help adjust the schedule — what times would work better going forward?
Teacher changeI can submit a request to review the teacher assignment and flag your feedback for a better fit.
CompensationGiven what you've described, you qualify for one additional lesson as a gesture to make this right.
Sample Call — schedule complaint, resolved on-callOutcome: Resolved, no referral requested
S
Umm Sara · ParentHonestly, the class time hasn't worked for us in weeks — Sara's been missing half of them.
R
Rania · AgentThank you for telling me — I want to fix this properly rather than just note it. I can help adjust the schedule now. What times would actually work going forward?
S
Umm Sara · ParentEvenings after 7pm would be much better.
R
Rania · AgentI've updated that for you within the available options. We won't talk about referrals today — my priority is making sure this is actually fixed for Sara first.
5.7 · Outside permission scope

Escalation Script

This is something I want to make sure gets the right attention, so I'm escalating it directly to our CC / SS / Customer Service team today. You'll hear back within a few business days, and I'll personally note this so it isn't lost.

Rule: never promise an outcome outside the permissions in Section VI of the project doc (outbound tool, CRM query, referral registration, leave/make-up, class/teacher assistance, escalation mechanism). Escalate rather than guess.

Objections & FAQ

ObjectionResponse
"I don't have anyone in mind."That's fine — would a quick check-in or share work instead? No pressure either way.
"I already referred someone before."Thank you — is there anyone else who's come up since, or would you like me to check that referral's status?
"What do I get out of it?"Referrals that go on to attend and pay are rewarded under our current terms — I can confirm the exact details for your case.
"I'm not comfortable sharing their number."Understood — you're welcome to share our contact with them directly instead.
"Is this a sales call?"No — this is a service check for active families; referral only comes up if you're happy with the experience.
"I don't have time right now."No problem — is there a better time to call back, or should I just note that everything's going well?

Call Data Logging

  • Call outcome — connected / no answer / call back requested
  • If no answer: WhatsApp time-booking message sent
  • Satisfaction level captured
  • Main feedback (1–2 lines, free text)
  • Service issue identified, and type
  • Issue resolved on-call, escalated, or unresolved
  • Referral triggered — name/contact if provided
  • Check-in / share completed as fallback
  • Follow-up required, and by whom
10

Quick Reference Card

1. Start with: Was the call answered? Yes → Opening. No → WhatsApp time booking.

2. If answered, continue the existing workflow from Opening without changes.

3. Assess satisfaction across the 5 probe dimensions.

4. Satisfied → referral ask, or check-in/share if no referral.

5. Dissatisfied → resolve within permissions, or escalate.

6. Close with the matching script, then log the call.

Golden rule: resolve before you ask — and never end a satisfied call empty-handed.
